# Measure Findings: CHG-04 Simplify Brand Buttons
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

The button hierarchy now uses yellow for primary actions and neutral surfaces for secondary controls. The compiled application passes automated checks. The result is a conditional local pass because post-change browser and responsive evidence has not been recorded.

## Acceptance Results

| Criterion | Result | Evidence or gap |
|---|---|---|
| Filled primary actions use the approved yellow | Pass locally | `application/source/resources/css/app.css` maps `--primary` and `--sidebar-primary` to `--brand-yellow: #eab41e`. |
| Secondary buttons and badges do not use the green fill | Pass locally | `--secondary` is neutral in light and dark themes; existing `Button` and `Badge` secondary variants inherit the neutral token without source rewrites. |
| Broad hover and active surfaces do not compete with primary actions | Pass locally | `--accent` and `--sidebar-accent` are neutral in light and dark themes. |
| Green remains available as a supporting brand accent | Pass locally | `--brand-green`, `--brand-green-dark`, chart tokens, and existing success text remain available for small supporting states. |
| Dark mode mappings compile | Pass locally; browser pending | `npm run build` passed and the compiled CSS contains both neutral light and dark token values. |
| Responsive visual behavior | Blocked for evidence | Manual desktop, tablet, and mobile review has not been run after the change. |
| Staging and launch acceptance | Not applicable to local build | Staging environment, operations, and authorized launch acceptance remain open project gates. |

## Open Gaps

- Run a post-change browser review for the welcome, dashboard, classroom, authentication, settings, focus, disabled, and destructive states.
- Review light mode and dark mode at desktop, tablet, and mobile widths.
- Record screenshots or reproducible visual notes before treating CHG-04 (Simplify the CHG-03 button hierarchy) as visually accepted.
- Keep staging and final LeadLab Director acceptance as separate launch gates.

## Decision Boundary

Measure result: **conditional local pass**. The neutral secondary treatment can continue to browser and staging validation, but this run does not accept the application for release or close the remaining launch gates.
